3-day-kakheti-wine-and-food-tour-from-tb.title: 3-Day Kakheti Wine and Food Tour from Tbilisi
3-day-kakheti-wine-and-food-tour-from-tb.description:
The 3-Day Kakheti Wine and Food Tour is a private trip from Tbilisi through Kakheti, Georgia's main wine region in the South Caucasus. Over three days you taste at both family-run wineries and larger wine estates, see the qvevri method that UNESCO recognizes as intangible cultural heritage, and visit the region's cultural landmarks — Tsinandali Estate, Gremi Fortress, the hilltop town of Sighnaghi and Bodbe Monastery — with traditional Georgian meals paired with local wine.

Three days is enough to go well beyond a day trip at a balanced pace, with tastings alongside food, old towns and quiet cultural sites — so it suits wine lovers and first-time visitors to Kakheti alike, on its own or as part of a longer route through Georgia. You stay two nights in Telavi, in the heart of the region, so daily drives stay short and you unpack once. Along the way you meet two kinds of producer: family wineries, where wine is still made in buried qvevri and hosted around a home table, and larger estates such as Tsinandali and Khareba — a contrast that's part of what makes the three days interesting.

Because it's private, the tour runs only for your group, with your own guide-driver, and the route, hotels and pace can be shaped around what you want. Hikasus Travel is a local team based in Georgia and handles the transport, hotels, guiding and logistics, so you can focus on the wine, food and the drive.

highlights: Private three-day route from Tbilisi into Kakheti, Georgia's main wine region
Six wine tastings across family wineries and larger estates
Qvevri winemaking — the UNESCO-listed method of fermenting wine in buried clay vessels
A tasting inside Khareba Winery's underground tunnels

itinerary.title: Day 1 — Tbilisi - Telavi - Tsinandali Estate - Local Winery - Telavi
itinerary.content:
You leave Tbilisi behind and cross into Kakheti over the Gombori Pass, visit the Tsinandali Estate, and have lunch and a tasting at a family winery before settling into Telavi for two nights.

You leave Tbilisi in the morning and head east into Kakheti over the Gombori Pass, a mountain road that eases you into the region's rural landscapes. Around midday you reach the Tsinandali Estate, a 19th-century estate with landscaped gardens, its own winery and a long winemaking history. From there you stop at a family-run winery for a traditional Georgian lunch paired with wines made on site. In the evening you arrive in Telavi and check in for the first of two nights.

  • Morning pick-up from your Tbilisi hotel
  • Drive east into Kakheti over the Gombori Pass
  • Visit the Tsinandali Estate and its gardens
  • Lunch and wine tasting at a family-run winery
  • Overnight in Telavi
  • Duration of the tour: 7-8 hours
  • Driving duration: 2.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 2 — Telavi - Vardisubani - Khareba Winery - Gremi - Napareuli - Telavi
itinerary.content:
A full day of traditional winemaking and local culture: qvevri wine in Vardisubani, a tasting in Khareba's rock-cut tunnels, the medieval Gremi Fortress, and a home-style dinner in Napareuli.

The day starts in the village of Vardisubani, where families still ferment wine in qvevris — large clay vessels set into the ground — for a close look at a method that goes back thousands of years. Next is Khareba Winery, where the tasting takes place inside tunnels carved into the rock. You then visit Gremi Fortress, a 16th-century royal citadel that overlooks the Alazani Valley. The day closes in the village of Napareuli with a traditional dinner and locally made wine, before you return to your hotel in Telavi.

  • Qvevri winemaking experience in Vardisubani
  • Wine tasting in Khareba Winery's underground tunnels
  • Visit the 16th-century Gremi Fortress
  • Traditional dinner with local wine in Napareuli
  • Overnight in Telavi
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 2 hours

itinerary.title: Day 3 — Telavi - Batonistsikhe - Sighnaghi - Bodbe - Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
Your last day takes in Batonistsikhe Castle in Telavi, the hilltop town of Sighnaghi and Bodbe Monastery, with a final tasting before the drive back to Tbilisi.

You begin at Batonistsikhe Castle, a former royal residence in Telavi, with time to walk through the town. From there you drive to Sighnaghi, a walled hilltop town of cobbled streets and painted houses known as the "City of Love," with wide views over the Alazani Valley. Nearby is Bodbe Monastery, a quiet complex set among cypress trees. Before heading back, you share a final dinner and wine tasting at a local winery, then return to Tbilisi.

  • Visit Batonistsikhe Castle and walk through Telavi
  • Explore Sighnaghi, the "City of Love," with views over the Alazani Valley
  • Visit Bodbe Monastery
  • Final dinner and wine tasting at a local winery
  • Return to Tbilisi
  • Duration of the tour: 10-11 hours
  • Driving duration: 4 hours

Gaze up at the towering cliffs, breathe in the fresh mountain air, and let the serenity of the canyon wash over you. Return to Kutaisi.

5-day-georgia-private-tour-tbilisi-wine-.title: 5-Day Georgia Private Tour: Tbilisi, Wine & Sulfur Baths
5-day-georgia-private-tour-tbilisi-wine-.description:
Mountains and wine in five days. This private loop from Tbilisi pairs the high Caucasus with the country's oldest wine region — monasteries and snow peaks one day, cellars and vineyards the next.

It opens gently in the capital, with a walk through the Old Town and a look at the sulfur bath district the city grew up around. Then you head north on the Georgian Military Highway, climbing past the monasteries of Mtskheta and the fortress at Ananuri to Kazbegi, a small town beneath the snows of Mount Kazbek and the lone church at Gergeti — the view most people picture when they think of Georgia.

From there it's east into Kakheti, where Georgians have made wine in clay for 8,000 years. You'll taste it at a grand old estate and inside a cellar tunnelled into a mountain, wander the walled hill town of Sighnaghi above the Alazani valley, and end back in Tbilisi.

The days are full and the driving is real, but each evening lands you somewhere new — and because it's private, the whole thing bends around you rather than the other way round.

You'll start at the vast Holy Trinity Cathedral, or Sameba, that rises over the skyline, then head into the Old Town — winding up its lanes to the Narikala fortress, crossing the Peace Bridge over the river, and walking through Abanotubani, the district of brick-domed sulfur bathhouses the city was built on and named after. North today, up the old Georgian Military Highway into the Caucasus. First stop is Mtskheta, Georgia's spiritual heart — the great Svetitskhoveli cathedral in the town, and Jvari monastery on the hill above it, both UNESCO sites. Then a pause at Ananuri, a fortress standing over the turquoise Jinvali reservoir, before the road climbs to Kazbegi, a small town under the snows of Mount Kazbek where the air changes completely.

An early start for Gergeti Trinity Church — the lone church on the hillside with Kazbek behind it, and the view most people come to Georgia for. It's best in the morning, before the cloud sets in. Then a long, scenic drive east into Kakheti, the wine country, with a stop at the old Tsinandali estate to taste in its gardens before settling into Telavi for the night.

The full wine day. It starts at Khareba, where the cellar is a tunnel cut straight into the mountainside and the tasting happens deep inside. Then Sighnaghi, a small walled town of red roofs above the Alazani valley, and Bodbe, the quiet convent just below it. Back to Tbilisi in the evening for your last night.

6-day-georgia-private-tour-highlights-fr.title: 6-Day Georgia Private Tour: Highlights from Tbilisi
6-day-georgia-private-tour-highlights-fr.seoTitle: 6-Day Georgia Private Tour: Highlights & Culture from Tbilisi
6-day-georgia-private-tour-highlights-fr.description:
Cave cities and cliff monasteries, in six days. This private loop runs west from Tbilisi through the heart of old Georgia — rock-hewn towns, a monastery dug into a mountainside, and two of the country's great medieval churches — before circling back to the capital.

You start in Tbilisi, then head west to the Iron Age caves of Uplistsikhe and the old spa town of Borjomi. From there it's up to Vardzia, a whole monastery carved into a cliff, and the rebuilt castle at Akhaltsikhe, before dropping down to Kutaisi and the green water of Martvili Canyon on the way home.

The thread running through it is stone — towns, churches and monasteries cut straight into the rock over the last three thousand years. Vardzia alone once held hundreds of rooms across up to thirteen levels, built into the mountain under Queen Tamar in the 12th century.

The days are full and the driving is real, but each evening lands you somewhere new — and because it's private, the whole thing bends around you rather than the other way round.

itinerary.title: Day 2: Tbilisi – Uplistsikhe – Gori – Borjomi
itinerary.content:
West today, into Georgia's older history. First is Uplistsikhe, a town cut straight into the rock that was a trading hub as far back as the Iron Age — you can walk its cave halls, tunnels and carved streets. Then a stop in Gori for the Stalin Museum, in the town where he was born, before you carry on to Borjomi, the old spa town known for its mineral water and the wooded Central Park in the hills above it.

  • Visit Uplistsikhe ancient rock-hewn town;
  • Explore cave dwellings and tunnels;
  • Visit Stalin Museum in Gori;
  • Travel to Borjomi;
  • Walk in Borjomi Central Park;
  • Taste famous Borjomi mineral water;
  • Overnight stay in Borjomi.
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 3.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 3: Borjomi – Vardzia – Akhaltsikhe
itinerary.content:
Today's the big one: Vardzia, a monastery carved into the side of the Erusheti mountain in the 12th century, under Queen Tamar. What's left is a honeycomb of rooms, tunnels and chapels spread across the cliff face, with a frescoed church still in use at its centre. Afterwards you'll head to Akhaltsikhe and its Rabati Castle, a rebuilt fortress where a mosque, a church and a synagogue stand inside the same walls — a good picture of how mixed this border region has always been.

  • Visit Vardzia cave monastery complex;
  • Explore medieval cave dwellings and churches;
  • Learn about Queen Tamar's legacy;
  • Travel to Akhaltsikhe;
  • Explore Rabati Castle fortress;
  • Discover diverse cultural heritage;
  • Overnight stay in Akhaltsikhe.
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 3 hours

itinerary.title: Day 4: Akhaltsikhe – Kutaisi
itinerary.content:
A drive west brings you to Kutaisi, one of Georgia's oldest cities, lived in for more than 3,000 years. Up on the hill sits Bagrati Cathedral, an 11th-century church rebuilt in recent years, looking out over the town. A short way out is the Gelati monastery, founded in the 12th century by King David the Builder and still on the UNESCO list — its main church is covered inside with medieval mosaics and frescoes. There's time to walk the city centre before your night in Kutaisi.

  • Scenic drive to Kutaisi;
  • Visit Bagrati Cathedral (UNESCO World Heritage Site);
  • Explore Gelati Monastery complex;
  • Discover medieval Georgian architecture;
  • Walk through Kutaisi city center;
  • Overnight stay in Kutaisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 7-8 hours
  • Driving duration: 3.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 5: Kutaisi – Martvili Canyon – Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
On the way back east you'll stop at Martvili Canyon, a narrow gorge of green water below mossy cliffs, with a short boat trip through the middle of it when conditions allow. It's an easy, pretty break before the long drive to Tbilisi, where the evening is yours for a last dinner or a wander.

  • Take boat trip through emerald waters;
  • Explore narrow gorge with lush vegetation;

  • Overnight stay in Tbilisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 4 hours

itinerary.title: Day 6: Departure from Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
A free morning, shaped around your flight — time for a last coffee, some souvenir shopping, or a slow breakfast. Then you'll check out and transfer to Tbilisi International Airport for the trip home.

  • Free time for last-minute exploration;
  • Hotel check-out;
  • Transfer to Tbilisi International Airport;
  • Departure from Georgia.

Explore the dynamic culture of the city, visit the famous sulfur baths, and stroll along Rustaveli Avenue. Experience the perfect blend of ancient history and modern vibrancy. Stop at the historic Ananuri Fortress overlooking the Zhinvali Reservoir, offering glimpses into Georgia's medieval past. Continue to Kazbegi (Stepantsminda), famous for dramatic mountain landscapes and the iconic Gergeti Trinity Church, perched on a hill with panoramic views of Mount Kazbek. 8-day-georgia-private-tour-culture-natur.title: 8-Day Georgia Private Tour: Culture, Nature & Wine
8-day-georgia-private-tour-culture-natur.seoTitle: 8-Day Georgia Private Tour: Culture, Nature & Wine from Tbilisi
8-day-georgia-private-tour-culture-natur.description:
Mountains, monasteries and wine, in eight days. This private trip from Tbilisi runs up to the high Caucasus at Kazbegi, then out into the Kakheti wine country, using a few fixed bases so you're not packing and unpacking every night.

You start in the capital and drive north over the Georgian Military Highway to Kazbegi, spending two nights under Mount Kazbek for the church at Gergeti and the Gveleti waterfall. Coming back through the cave town of Uplistsikhe and Gori, you return to Tbilisi and swing east into Kakheti for two days of wineries, hill towns and old estates, with a free day in the capital to finish.

Wine is the through-line of the second half. Georgians have made it in buried clay qvevri for around 8,000 years, and in Kakheti you'll taste it where it's made — from a grand 19th-century estate to small family cellars.

Some days are long and the driving is real, but the mountains and the wine country are the two things most people come to Georgia for — and because it's private, the pace and the stops bend around you.
8-day-georgia-private-tour-culture-natur.metaDescription: Immerse yourself in the best of Georgia's cultural heritage, breathtaking landscapes, and celebrated wine traditions on this 8-day tour.

itinerary.title: Day 1: Arrival and City Tour in Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
Arrive, settle in, and spend the afternoon in Tbilisi. You'll walk the Old Town's cobbled lanes, stop at Holy Trinity Cathedral — the huge Sameba that anchors the skyline — and ride up to the Narikala fortress for the view across the rooftops. Down by the river you'll cross the Peace Bridge, with the evening free to get a first taste of Georgian food and wine.

  • Arrival in Tbilisi and hotel check-in;
  • Explore Tbilisi Old Town;
  • Visit Holy Trinity Cathedral;
  • See Narikala Fortress;
  • Walk across Peace Bridge;
  • Discover local culture and cuisine;
  • Overnight stay in Tbilisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 4-5 hours
  • Driving duration: 30 minutes

itinerary.title: Day 2: Tbilisi – Jvari – Mtskheta – Ananuri – Kazbegi
itinerary.content:
North today, up the old Georgian Military Highway into the Caucasus. You'll stop in Mtskheta, Georgia's spiritual heart — the 11th-century Svetitskhoveli cathedral in the town and, on the hill above, the 6th-century Jvari monastery, both UNESCO sites. Further up, the Ananuri fortress sits over the turquoise Jinvali reservoir, a good place to break the drive before the road climbs to Kazbegi, a small town under the snows of Mount Kazbek.

  • Visit Jvari Monastery (UNESCO World Heritage Site);
  • Explore Mtskheta and Svetitskhoveli Cathedral;
  • Stop at Ananuri Architectural Complex;
  • Enjoy views of Jinvali Reservoir;
  • Arrive in Stepantsminda (Kazbegi);
  • Overnight stay in Kazbegi.
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 3.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 3: Kazbegi – Gergeti Trinity Church – Gveleti Waterfall – Kazbegi
itinerary.content:
A day in the mountains, with the same base for the night. The morning goes to Gergeti Trinity, the lone church at about 2,170 metres with Mount Kazbek rising behind it — one of the country's great views, and best before the cloud comes in. Later you'll walk out to the Gveleti waterfall, a short hike into clean mountain air and cold, clear water, before heading back to Kazbegi.

  • Visit Gergeti Trinity Church;
  • Enjoy panoramic views of Mount Kazbek;
  • Hike to Gveleti Waterfall;
  • Experience pristine mountain nature;
  • Photography opportunities;
  • Return to Kazbegi;
  • Overnight stay in Kazbegi.
  • Duration of the tour: 6-7 hours
  • Driving duration: 1 hour

itinerary.title: Day 4: Kazbegi – Uplistsikhe – Gori – Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
You leave the mountains and head back towards Tbilisi, with two stops on the way. First is Uplistsikhe, a town cut straight into the rock, with cave halls and tunnels that go back to the Iron Age. Then Gori, and its Stalin Museum, in the town where he was born — a museum that has stayed much the same since Soviet times. You reach Tbilisi in the evening.

  • Depart Kazbegi;
  • Explore Uplistsikhe ancient cave town;
  • Visit Stalin Museum in Gori;
  • Learn about Georgian archaeological heritage;
  • Return to Tbilisi;
  • Overnight stay in Tbilisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 9-10 hours
  • Driving duration: 5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 5: Tbilisi – Telavi – Lunch and Wine Tasting at the Winery – Tsinandali – Telavi
itinerary.content:
East into Kakheti today, Georgia's main wine region. You'll reach Telavi, the region's main town, and sit down to lunch with a tasting at a local winery — a proper introduction to how Georgians make wine in buried clay qvevri. In the afternoon you'll visit the Tsinandali estate, the 19th-century home and gardens of Prince Alexander Chavchavadze, whose cellar still holds bottles more than a century old. The night is in Telavi.

  • Travel to Kakheti wine region;
  • Arrive in Telavi;
  • Lunch and wine tasting at local winery;
  • Visit Tsinandali Estate and gardens;
  • Learn about Georgian wine traditions;
  • Overnight stay in Telavi.

itinerary.title: Day 6: Telavi – Sighnaghi – Bodbe – Dinner and Wine Tasting at the Winery – Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
More of Kakheti today. First is Sighnaghi, a small walled town of red roofs and balconies on a ridge above the Alazani valley — an easy place to wander for a while. Just below sits Bodbe, the convent built around the grave of St Nino, who brought Christianity to Georgia in the 4th century. You'll end with dinner and a last tasting at a local winery before the drive back to Tbilisi.

  • Visit Sighnaghi, the "City of Love";
  • Explore Bodbe Monastery;
  • Learn about St. Nino's legacy;
  • Enjoy dinner and wine tasting;
  • Experience Kakheti wine traditions;
  • Return to Tbilisi;
  • Overnight stay in Tbilisi.
  • Duration of the tour: 9-10 hours
  • Driving duration: 3.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 7: Free Day in Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
A free day to take Tbilisi at your own pace. Go back to the spots you liked, try the sulfur baths in the old town, poke around the markets and galleries, or just sit in a courtyard café and do very little. It's your day to see the city the way you want.

8-day-georgia-culture-and-adventure-tour.title: 8-Day Georgia Culture & Adventure Tour
8-day-georgia-culture-and-adventure-tour.description:
The 8-Day Georgia Culture and Adventure Tour is a private trip from Tbilisi that pairs Georgia's cultural highlights with active days outdoors, across the South Caucasus. In eight days you cover Tbilisi, the wine region of Kakheti, the UNESCO monuments of Mtskheta, the cave town of Uplistsikhe and the high Caucasus around Kazbegi, with a full-day hike in Lagodekhi National Park and rafting on the way north.

Tbilisi is the hub — you're based there for four of the seven nights, with single nights in Lagodekhi, Telavi and Kazbegi.
8-day-georgia-culture-and-adventure-tour.listingDescription: Dive into the wonders of Georgia on this 8-day adventure, blending cultural discovery, historic landmarks, and exhilarating outdoor activities.

itinerary.title: Day 1 — Arrival and city tour in Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
Your driver meets you and transfers you to your hotel, and your guide then leads a walking tour of the old town. You start at Holy Trinity Cathedral (Sameba), one of the largest Orthodox churches in the world, then visit Metekhi Church and the monument to Vakhtang Gorgasali, the city's founder. A cable car takes you up to Narikala Fortress for views over the city, and from there you walk down to Abanotubani, the district known for its domed sulfur bathhouses, passing the small Leghvtakhevi Waterfall. You continue into the Sharden area, with its cafés, wine bars and shops, and see Sioni Cathedral, Anchiskhati Basilica and the clock tower of the Rezo Gabriadze Theater. The walk finishes across the Bridge of Peace to Rike Park. In the evening you have dinner at a traditional Georgian restaurant. Overnight in Tbilisi.

  • Guided old-town tour: Holy Trinity Cathedral, Metekhi Church and the Vakhtang Gorgasali monument
  • Cable car to Narikala Fortress, then down through Abanotubani's sulfur-bath district past Leghvtakhevi Waterfall
  • The Sharden area, Sioni Cathedral, Anchiskhati Basilica and the Gabriadze Theater clock tower
  • Across the Bridge of Peace to Rike Park
  • Dinner at a traditional Georgian restaurant; overnight in Tbilisi
  • Duration of the tour: 4-5 hours
  • Driving duration: 30 minutes

itinerary.title: Day 2 — Tbilisi – Bodbe – Sighnaghi – Lagodekhi
itinerary.content:
You leave Tbilisi and drive east into Kakheti, Georgia's main wine region. Your first stop is Bodbe Monastery, a quiet religious site with views over the valley. You then explore Sighnaghi, the walled hilltop town known as the "City of Love," with cobbled streets, painted houses and wide views over the Alazani Valley. Lunch and a wine tasting follow at a local winery nearby. In the late afternoon you continue to Lagodekhi, check into your hotel and have a relaxed evening in the mountain town. Overnight in Lagodekhi.

  • Bodbe Monastery, above the Alazani Valley
  • Sighnaghi, the "City of Love," with valley views
  • Lunch and wine tasting at a local winery
  • Drive to Lagodekhi; overnight
  • Duration of the tour: 7-8 hours
  • Driving duration: 3 hours

itinerary.title: Day 3 — Lagodekhi – Hiking in Lagodekhi National Park – Telavi
itinerary.content:
You spend the day hiking in Lagodekhi National Park, on a scenic route through forest and past waterfalls, with lunch boxes provided. After around five hours on the trail you drive to Telavi, the main town of Kakheti's wine country, where you have dinner with local wine and stay the night. Overnight in Telavi.

  • A guided hike in Lagodekhi National Park (about 5 hours), lunch boxes provided
  • Drive to Telavi
  • Dinner with local wine; overnight in Telavi
  • Duration of the tour: 7-8 hours
  • Driving duration: 1.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 4 — Telavi – Vardisubani – Cooking Master-Classes – Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
You start with a short walk in Telavi, visiting the Telavi Historical Museum and Batonistsikhe Fortress. You then take part in a cooking master-class with local chefs, learning to prepare traditional Georgian dishes, followed by lunch paired with Georgian wine. In the afternoon you drive back to Tbilisi over the scenic Gombori Pass, arriving in the evening. Overnight in Tbilisi.

  • Telavi Historical Museum and Batonistsikhe Fortress
  • Georgian cooking master-class with local chefs, then lunch with wine
  • Drive to Tbilisi over the Gombori Pass; overnight
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 3 hours

itinerary.title: Day 5 — Tbilisi – Jvari – Mtskheta – Uplistsikhe – Dinner at the winery – Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
You explore Georgia's historical and spiritual heartland. You begin at Jvari Monastery, set on a hill above the meeting of two rivers, then visit Mtskheta, Georgia's ancient capital and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, home to Svetitskhoveli Cathedral. Later you drive to Uplistsikhe, a cave town carved into the rock that shows early Georgian building and daily life. You return to Tbilisi in the late afternoon, and in the evening have dinner and a wine tasting at a local winery. Overnight in Tbilisi.

  • Jvari Monastery, above the confluence of two rivers
  • Mtskheta and Svetitskhoveli Cathedral (UNESCO World Heritage)
  • The cave town of Uplistsikhe
  • Dinner and wine tasting at a winery in Tbilisi; overnight
  • Duration of the tour: 9-10 hours
  • Driving duration: 3.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 6 — Tbilisi – Rafting – Ananuri – Kazbegi
itinerary.content:
The day begins with rafting on the Pshavi Aragvi River, a lively way to start the drive north into the mountains. Afterwards you visit Ananuri Fortress, a medieval complex of towers and churches above the Zhinvali Reservoir. Continuing along the Georgian Military Road, you stop at the Gudauri panorama viewpoint for wide mountain views, then arrive in Kazbegi and check into your hotel among the peaks. The evening is free. Overnight in Kazbegi.

  • Rafting on the Pshavi Aragvi River
  • Ananuri Fortress, above the Zhinvali Reservoir
  • The Gudauri panorama viewpoint
  • Arrive in Kazbegi; overnight
  • Duration of the tour: 8-9 hours
  • Driving duration: 4 hours

itinerary.title: Day 7 — Kazbegi – Gergeti Trinity Church – Gori – Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
You drive up into the mountains to Gergeti Trinity Church, which stands on a hill with Mount Kazbek behind it — one of Georgia's best-known views. After time at the church you continue south to Gori to visit the Stalin Museum, dedicated to the Soviet leader who was born in the town, which gives some insight into a complex part of the country's history. In the late afternoon you drive back to Tbilisi. Overnight in Tbilisi.

  • Gergeti Trinity Church, below Mount Kazbek
  • The Stalin Museum in Gori
  • Drive back to Tbilisi; overnight
  • Duration of the tour: 9-10 hours
  • Driving duration: 5.5 hours

itinerary.title: Day 8 — Departure from Tbilisi
itinerary.content:
After check-out, your driver transfers you to Tbilisi International Airport for departure, with some free time in the morning beforehand depending on your flight time.

  • Hotel check-out and transfer to Tbilisi International Airport
  • End of the tour

Conclude your ultimate 20-day Georgian adventure with transfer from Batumi to Tbilisi International Airport for departure. Carry with you unforgettable memories of Georgia's cultural heritage, scenic landscapes, culinary delights, wine traditions, mountain trekking adventures, and the perfect balance of history, nature, and total relaxation that defines this extraordinary land of diverse regions and warm hospitality.

  • Transfer from Batumi to Tbilisi Airport;
  • Final departure from Georgian adventure;
  • Memories of cultural heritage exploration;
  • Scenic landscapes and culinary delights;
  • Wine traditions and mountain trekking;
  • Perfect balance of history and nature;
  • End of 20-day comprehensive journey.
  • Duration: As per flight schedule
  • Driving duration: 5.5 hours to airport

included: Accommodation in double or twin rooms, with breakfast included;
Transfers as per the itinerary in a comfortable, air-conditioned vehicle, with an English-speaking guide driver;
